chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who cut off the head of a dead man, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah (Exalted and Majestic) sanctified the dead from it just as He sanctified the living from it. So whoever does with the dead an act that would be a violation of the living soul if done to the living, upon him is the blood money (diyah).'

So I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about that, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) spoke truthfully. Thus spoke the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' I said: 'So whoever cuts off the head of a dead man, or pierces his belly, or does with him what constitutes a violation of the living soul, is upon him the complete blood money of the soul?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but its blood money is the blood money of the foetus in the belly of its mother, before the spirit is breathed into it, and that is one hundred dinars, and it is for its inheritors, while the blood money of this one (the dead man) is for him, not for the inheritors.'

I said: 'So what is the difference between the two?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The foetus is a matter of the future, its benefit is hoped for, and this one has passed and its benefit has gone. So when he is mutilated after his death, his blood money becomes for the mutilation for him, not for someone else. It is used to perform Hajj on his behalf, and the doors of goodness and righteousness are opened with it, from charity or other than it.'

I said: 'So if a man intends to dig a grave for him in order to wash him in the grave, and the man shovels from what he digs, and the shovel in his hand touches his belly so it pierces it, so what is upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is like that, so it is a mistake (accidental), and its expiation is the freeing of a neck, or fasting for two consecutive months, or charity upon sixty poor people, a Mudd for each poor person, by the Mudd of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.اجْتِيَاحُ النَّفْسِ: Violation or desecration of the soul/body
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or financial compensation for injury or death
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation or atonement for a sin or mistake
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A traditional unit of volume for measuring food, used here for charity

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for cutting off the head of a dead man according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of *diyah* for mutilating a corpse, distinguishing it from killing a living person by assigning a fixed compensation of one hundred dinars that remains with the deceased for their own spiritual merit, such as Hajj or charity, rather than going to heirs. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and Imam al-Rida (AS) clarify that this distinction arises because the deceased has passed, whereas the fetus is a future expectation; furthermore, accidental injury during burial rites incurs the standard expiation for accidental death, reflecting the principle of *khata'*. This ruling underscores the Shia view of the deceased's continued agency in receiving spiritual rewards through their estate.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Hafs, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man who cut off the head of a dead man. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Sanctified from it for a dead just as He<sup>azwj</sup> has Sanctified from it for a living. So the one who deals with a dead with a deed which violates it is similar to violating a living. Thus, upon him would be the wergild’.

So I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> spoke truthfully. Such is what Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said’. I said, ‘So the one who cut of the head of a dead, or pierces his belly, or does with him what happens to be a violation in it of a living soul, so upon him is the complete wergild of the soul?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but its wergild is the wergild of the foetus which is in the belly of its mother, before the spirit is Breathed into it, and that is one hundred Dinars, and it is for its (foetus’s) inheritors, while the wergild of this one (deceased), it is for him, not for his inheritors.

I said, ‘So what is the difference between the two?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The foetus is a matter of the future, its benefit is hoped for, and this one has passed and its benefit has gone. So when his is tortured with after his death, his wergild comes to be for the torture of his, not for someone else. It (wergild) would be utilised for performing Hajj with it on his behalf, and would be done with it from the doors of goodness and the righteousness, from charity or other than it.’

I said, ‘So if a man intends that he digs a grave for him in order to wash him in his grave, so the man shovel from what he digs, and the shovel in his hand touches his belly so it pierces. So what would be upon him?’ So heasws said: ‘When it is like that, so it is a mistake, and its expiation is the freeing of a neck, or Fasting for two months consecutively, or charity upon sixty poor ones, a handful (Mudd) for each poor, by a handful (Mudd) of the Prophetsaww’.
